issues.description: SealSaloon constructor signature is inconsistent across artifacts: the problem statement/UML specifies `SealSaloon(String)` (saloon name for identification), but the provided solution implements only a no-argument constructor `SealSaloon()`. The template's Main example also instantiates `new SealSaloon()` (commented). Students following the statement will implement a String-parameter constructor, while the provided solution/example suggests otherwise, potentially breaking tests or confusing required API.
issues.suggestedFix: Align all artifacts to the same constructor API. Prefer implementing `public SealSaloon(String name)` as specified (store the name in a private field with a getter). Update the Main example accordingly; optionally keep `SealSaloon()` delegating to `this("")` if backward compatibility is desired.

issues.description: The UML diagram lists `acceptSupplyDelivery(String,int,int)` and `calculateTotalPrice(Meal)` as instance methods (no static marker), but the written instructions explicitly require `acceptSupplyDelivery`, `calculateTotalPrice`, and the `stock` attribute to be static. This inconsistency makes it unclear whether students should implement and call these as instance methods or class (static) methods.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the UML consistent with the text by marking `stock`, `acceptSupplyDelivery`, and `calculateTotalPrice` as static in the diagram, or remove the static requirement from the text and keep them instance-level (then update the solution accordingly).
